headline: High-risk workspace-to-document pipeline: shared workspace state and file I/O create medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI can ingest workspace pages and databases, and unstructured reads/writes documents in a Docker container. Because A shares workspace state across instances and B processes documents, content from A can be reintroduced into B as attacker-controlled text in default workflows. No provenance tracking is documented, so the interaction is plausible and not blocked.
conditions: IF A-generated workspace content is exported into documents that B parses as instructions or metadata
IF B ingests files originating from the shared workspace without provenance filtering
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all A-generated exports before B ingests them
Restrict B to a quarantine folder for A-originated files
Require a human review step before B processes workspace-derived documents
Disable any instruction-following behavior on document text in B
requires-engineering: implement content provenance checks between the two systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while B can read and write documents from the filesystem. The pair therefore has a default shared-data path where workspace content can be copied into B’s local processing context and potentially leave the workspace boundary. No explicit isolation or redaction is documented, so leakage risk is real but not clearly catastrophic.
conditions: IF workspace pages are exported into files that B processes
IF B outputs derived documents containing copied workspace content
mitigations: Limit B to non-sensitive sample documents
Redact secrets before export from A
Store B inputs in a separate directory with access controls
Review B outputs before re-importing into the workspace
requires-engineering: add automatic sensitive-data filtering on the export path

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has shared workspace state across instances, and B supports multiple instances with filesystem write access. Even though A cannot write the host filesystem, both can mutate overlapping document/workspace artifacts through different surfaces, creating race and overwrite risk in default collaborative use. The profiles do not show locking or coordination primitives.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same exported document set or workspace-derived files
IF concurrent runs modify the same artifact without external locking
mitigations: Run only one agent at a time on shared artifacts
Separate input and output directories
Use file-level locks during processing
Snapshot files before B writes results
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level coordination and locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a RAG-style workspace Q&A system, and B is a document-processing pipeline that can transform files. If B consumes A’s generated summaries or extracted text as authoritative input, errors or hallucinations from A can cascade into B’s outputs. No verification step is documented between them, so the default interaction is vulnerable.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated summaries or answers as source text
IF no independent verification step checks A’s claims before B transforms them
mitigations: Require source-document cross-checking before B acts on A output
Mark A output as untrusted in B’s pipeline
Add a human verification step for high-impact documents
Keep A and B in separate stages with explicit validation gates
requires-engineering: implement citation and provenance validation

E_compliance.rationale: A is vendor-hosted and sends workspace content to Notion vendor backends, while B is a local Docker-based open-source processor with allowlisted egress. The main compliance issue is a potential residency or retention mismatch if regulated workspace content is exported from A into B and then sent onward, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated data class or a documented policy conflict. Uncertainty keeps this low.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in A’s workspace and exported to B
IF B’s allowlisted egress sends that data to a third-party endpoint
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workflow
Check retention settings before export
Keep B offline for sensitive documents
Document the data flow for compliance review
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems
